logic_errors.title: Post-verification record-listing failure incorrectly enters remote recovery and masks the durable outcome
logic_errors.detail: After readSaved durably transitions the journal to VERIFIED, this.result() lists engine records outside publication error handling. If names()/readdirSync throws at that point, commit's broad catch treats this local publication/result failure as a remote execution failure and calls readSaved again. The second call attempts VERIFIED -> VERIFYING, which the journal correctly rejects. commit therefore rejects with Invalid transition instead of retaining a usable VERIFIED result with stale publication state; the original storage error is also lost. publish's sequence-directory listing is likewise outside its storage-write try/catch. No duplicate mutation was observed, and the durable VERIFIED journal state remains intact.
logic_errors.reproduction: In a copied synthetic fixture, replace CompletionRecordStore.prototype.names with a wrapper that throws once when the fixture journal first reaches VERIFIED. Configure refreshCache. commit rejects with Invalid transition; the journal remains VERIFIED, submit count is exactly one, and refreshCache is never called. The dedicated regression probe passed by asserting this current erroneous behavior.
logic_errors.recommendation: Separate local result/publication work from the mutation/readback recovery catch. Once a remote outcome transition succeeds, do not call readSaved again for local publication/result errors. Handle publication enumeration together with publication persistence, preserving the established outcome and explicitly stale publication state. Add the injected names()/readdir failure regression at both initial post-verification result construction and publication sequence enumeration.

confirmedProperties: Existing same-account/task/target preparation is replayed without issuing a replacement capability; queued commits serialize through PortalCoordinator.
Capability consumption is persisted and fsynced before durable SUBMIT_INTENT and before submit; consumption failures burn the ephemeral capability. Journal write failures poison subsequent writes.
Recovered submit/upload intent and uncertain outcomes permit read-only reconciliation, not submit/upload replay; tests cover submit/upload uncertainty and recovered journal boundaries.
Cancellation before submission is durably terminal at queue, preflight and stage boundaries; cancellation after submit does not claim rollback or repeat mutation.
The sealed full-policy digest is checked before preflight and again after stage; current trusted clock/freshness is assessed again immediately before consumption.
Absent, false or throwing host source verifier blocks before staging/submission.

Ordinary cache/projection callback failures and notification enqueue/transport failures preserve remote outcomes and do not authorize mutation retries. Local result/publication enumeration failures have the specific exception-boundary defect reported above.

Notification payloads are restricted, outcome IDs are deterministic, sender acknowledgements require matching IDs, malformed receipts fail closed, and persisted receipts suppress acknowledged replay. Unacknowledged transport may replay and requires sender-side ID deduplication.
Historical SAVED_WITH_DISCREPANCY latches the account circuit even after later reconciliation; unresolved intent/unknown latest states block other commits.

limitations: The engine is not registered/live and actual enrollment remains unmet, as specified in the task. Synthetic enrollment and source-verifier fixtures are not proof of real authorization or source integration.

summary: Focused synthetic safety tests pass (95 tests), with no identified duplicate remote mutation or enrollment/source-verifier bypass.
